prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) First, the class voted on which animal to sponsor through the zoo's adopt-an-animal program. (2) They chose a red panda named Juniper. (3) To raise the fifty dollars, students sold bookmarks they had designed themselves. (4) In May, the zoo sent the class a certificate and a photo of Juniper eating bamboo.
choices: Red pandas live in cool mountain forests in Asia and eat mostly bamboo leaves.
Ms. Cole's class found a creative way to support an animal at the city zoo.
Ms. Cole's class learned how zookeepers prepare food for the animals.
Selling bookmarks is a good way for a class to raise money for a trip.
why_wrong: introduces red pandas in general, but the paragraph is about what the class did
promises a paragraph about zookeepers' work, which the paragraph never describes
picks one detail (the bookmarks) and changes its purpose to a trip
explanation: The paragraph tells how one class sponsored a zoo animal, step by step. Only that sentence names the whole subject. The others focus on red pandas, on zookeepers, or on one detail with the wrong purpose.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) Rain gardens are small gardens planted in low spots of a yard. (2) When it storms, rainwater from roofs and driveways flows into them instead of into the street. (3) The plants' roots and the loose soil soak up the water and filter out dirt and oil. (4) This keeps the water that reaches streams and lakes cleaner.
choices: Rain gardens should be planted with flowers that bloom in many different colors.
Rainwater from roofs and driveways often carries dirt and oil into the street.
A rain garden is a simple way for a family to help keep local water clean.
A rain garden needs to be watered every day during a dry summer.
why_wrong: turns to how a rain garden should look, which the paragraph never discusses
repeats one detail instead of summing up
adds a new claim about watering instead of closing the explanation
explanation: The paragraph explains how rain gardens clean water. The best conclusion sums that up. The other choices discuss flower color, repeat a single detail, or bring in a new claim.

prompt: Which sentence would best support the claim in sentence 1 if it were added after sentence 3?
passage: (1) Our class should take its spring field trip to the science museum instead of the amusement park. (2) The museum is only twenty minutes from school by bus. (3) It also has a free lunch room for school groups.
choices: The amusement park has added a new roller coaster that goes faster than any other one in the state.
Some students in our class have already visited the science museum with their families.
The museum's new space exhibit connects to the solar system unit we are studying in science.
The science museum was built more than eighty years ago in the center of the city.
why_wrong: gives a reason to choose the amusement park, the opposite of the claim
gives a fact that, if anything, is a reason not to go
adds a fact about the building's age that gives no reason to choose it
explanation: The claim is that the class should choose the museum. A link to what the class is studying is a reason to go. The other choices favor the amusement park, weaken the claim, or give an unrelated fact.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) For three weeks, our class kept track of how much food was thrown away in the cafeteria. (2) On pizza days, students threw away very little. (3) On days when the cafeteria served steamed vegetables, the trash cans filled with uneaten broccoli and carrots. (4) In a survey, most students said they would eat more vegetables if they were served raw with a dip.
choices: Pizza is the most popular lunch in our cafeteria, and students almost never waste it.
Changing how vegetables are served might cut down on the food our cafeteria wastes.
Broccoli and carrots are two of the healthiest vegetables a person can eat.
Our class learned that the cafeteria throws away more food than any other school in the city.
why_wrong: builds a conclusion on one detail and overstates it
switches to nutrition, which the paragraph is not about
claims a comparison with other schools that the paragraph never made
explanation: The paragraph's findings point to one idea: serving vegetables differently could reduce waste. The other choices repeat one detail, change the subject, or claim something the class never measured.

prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) First, rinse the bottle and cut a hole the size of a coin in one side. (2) Next, push a wooden spoon through two smaller holes below it so the birds have a perch. (3) Then fill the bottle with seeds and screw the cap on tightly. (4) Finally, tie a string around the neck and hang the feeder from a sturdy branch.
choices: A plastic bottle can be turned into a bird feeder in four simple steps.
Many backyard birds, such as finches and sparrows, depend on seeds in the winter.
Plastic bottles can take hundreds of years to break down in a landfill.
A wooden spoon makes the best perch because birds can grip it easily.
why_wrong: introduces bird diets, but the paragraph gives instructions
introduces plastic waste, which the paragraph never discusses
introduces only one step of the process
explanation: The paragraph gives four steps for making a feeder, so the introduction should name that task. The others introduce bird diets, plastic waste, or a single step.

prompt: Which sentence would best support the claim in sentence 1 if it were added after sentence 2?
passage: (1) Students at Lakeview Middle School should be allowed to listen to music with headphones during independent work time. (2) Many students say quiet background music helps them block out noise from the hallway. (3) Teachers could still ask students to remove their headphones during lessons.
choices: In a survey of our seventh graders, most said they finished more work when they could listen to music.
Some students prefer songs with lyrics, while others like instrumental music, and they often argue about which is better.
Headphones have become much less expensive over the past ten years.
Music classes at Lakeview meet twice a week in the band room.
why_wrong: describes students' tastes in music, which says nothing about whether music helps them work
gives a fact about price that does not support the claim
mentions music classes, which have nothing to do with independent work time
explanation: The claim is that music should be allowed during independent work. Survey evidence that students finish more work with music supports it. The other choices discuss music tastes, prices, or music classes.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) The city's new bike-share program placed 200 bikes at stations around downtown. (2) Riders unlock a bike with a phone app and return it to any station. (3) In the first month, residents took more than 15,000 rides. (4) Many riders said they used the bikes for short trips they used to make by car.
choices: Riders who forget to return a bike to a station can be charged a fine, which some riders say is unfair.
The program's early numbers suggest that many residents are willing to trade short car trips for bikes.
Bicycles were invented in Europe more than two hundred years ago.
The program will soon expand to every neighborhood in the city because it has been so successful.
why_wrong: adds a new detail about fines instead of closing the paragraph
adds a history fact that has nothing to do with the program
announces an expansion the paragraph never mentions
explanation: The paragraph reports early results: many rides, often replacing car trips. The best conclusion draws that together. The others add a new detail, an unrelated fact, or an unsupported prediction.

prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) Students who type their notes can record more words, because most people type faster than they write. (2) However, students who write by hand often remember more of the lesson. (3) Writing slowly forces them to choose the most important ideas and put them in their own words. (4) For that reason, some teachers ask students to put their laptops away during lectures.
choices: Laptops can be expensive, so not every student has one to bring to class.
Students should always take notes by hand, because typing notes on a laptop is simply a waste of class time.
Typing and writing notes by hand each have an advantage, and the two help students in different ways.
Most teachers give lectures that last about twenty minutes.
why_wrong: introduces the cost of laptops, which the paragraph never discusses
takes one side completely, which contradicts the advantage of typing in sentence 1
introduces lecture length, which the paragraph never discusses
explanation: The paragraph weighs an advantage of typing against an advantage of handwriting. The introduction should present both. The others change the subject or deny the advantage the paragraph gives typing.

prompt: Which sentence would best support the claim in sentence 1 if it were added after sentence 2?
passage: (1) Our town should plant more trees along Main Street. (2) Trees make a street more pleasant for people walking to shops. (3) A local nursery has offered to sell the town young trees at a discount.
choices: Main Street has had the same shops for many years, including a hardware store.
Some trees lose all their leaves in the fall, while others stay green all year.
Shade from trees keeps sidewalks cooler on hot days.
Planting a single large tree can cost the town several hundred dollars.
why_wrong: describes the street's shops without giving a reason to plant trees
gives a general fact about trees that is not a reason to plant them
raises a cost, which works against the claim
explanation: The claim is that the town should plant trees. Cooler sidewalks are a benefit and a reason to plant them. The other choices describe the shops, state a general fact, or raise a cost.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) For decades, the town of Elm Ridge had a single bus line, which carried workers to the factory district. (2) When the town added two new routes last year, ridership doubled within six months. (3) Business owners near the new stops reported more customers on weekdays. (4) The town now plans a third route to the hospital and the community college.
choices: The factory district was built near the river in the early 1900s, long before the buses.
Better bus service has helped Elm Ridge's riders and its businesses alike.
Bus drivers in Elm Ridge must complete six weeks of training before driving a route.
Some residents still prefer to drive, because buses can be slow in winter weather.
why_wrong: adds a history fact unrelated to the new routes
adds a detail about drivers that the paragraph never develops
introduces an opposing point at the very end instead of concluding
explanation: The paragraph shows that new routes brought more riders and more customers. The best conclusion sums up both benefits. The others add unrelated facts or open a new point.
